subject: science
intro: A population is all the members of one species living in the same area. Populations depend on resources such as food, water, space, and shelter. When resources are plentiful, a population can grow. When resources become scarce, competition increases and the population may shrink. Scientists analyze data (like population counts over time) to find the effects of changing resources. Limiting factors are resources or conditions that restrict how large a population can grow.

items.prompt: A graph shows a deer population rising for several years, then falling sharply after a drought killed many plants. What caused the fall?

steps: Deer depend on plants for food.
The drought reduced the food supply, a key resource.
With less food, competition rose and many deer could not survive, so the population fell.
solution.answer: The drought reduced food (a resource), so the deer population fell.

items.prompt: Two populations of fish live in ponds of the same size. One pond has twice the food. Predict which population will likely be larger and why.

steps: More food means the resource supply is greater.
A greater food supply supports more individuals.
So the population in the pond with more food will likely be larger.
solution.answer: The population with more food will likely be larger, because food supports more individuals.

items.prompt: Define a limiting factor and give an example for a plant population.

steps: A limiting factor is a resource or condition that restricts population growth.
For plants, sunlight, water, or space can be limiting factors.
If one runs low, the plant population cannot keep growing.
solution.answer: A limiting factor restricts growth; for plants, water (or sunlight, space) is an example.
